bib.title: TL;DR: Mining Reddit to Learn Automatic Summarization
bib.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on New Frontiers in Summarization (NFiS), EMNLP 2017, pages 59-63

question: Can author-provided TL;DR summaries in social media posts be mined at scale into a training corpus for abstractive summarization beyond the news genre?
hypothesis: Social media posts with appended TL;DR lines give text-summary pairs written by the same person, usable to train summarizers; the technique should transfer to other sites and web crawls.
contributions: A method for mining author-provided summaries via the TL;DR convention
The Webis-TLDR-17 corpus of about 4 million content-summary pairs from Reddit
Corpus statistics and heuristic verticals (true summaries, question summaries, vulgar summaries)

method.summary: A five-step filtering pipeline over the Pushshift Reddit dump finds posts containing TL;DR spelling variants, removes bot accounts, splits each post at the TL;DR into content and summary, and applies length rules. A 1000-pair manual check estimates precision.
method.task: dataset construction for single-document abstractive summarization

datasets.name: Reddit crawl (Pushshift)
datasets.preprocessing: regex tl.{0,3}dr then 33 manually chosen spelling variants, bot removal, split at TL;DR

datasets.name: Webis-TLDR-17
datasets.size: about 4 million content-summary pairs (1,667,129 submissions, 2,377,372 comments, 32,778 subreddits)
datasets.preprocessing: drop multiple TL;DRs, summary must be shorter than content, content at least 2 words, summary at least 1 word; Markdown and inline URLs ignored when searching; a subset with 100-word content threshold is provided

models.name: Rush et al. (2015) and Nallapati et al. (2016) models

other.note: only mentioned as preliminary experiments; no settings given

inference.samples: one pass over the corpus; 1000 randomly selected pairs reviewed manually

parameters.spelling_variants_kept: 33 of the 100 most frequent (covering 90% of the distribution)
parameters.question_words: 21 English question words plus a question mark
parameters.vulgar_word_list: more than 500 words, Google What Do You Love project

metrics.name: precision of pairs
metrics.definition: share of 1000 random pairs judged correct by manual review

eval.protocol: manual review of 1000 randomly selected pairs; reviewer count and criteria not stated; no quantitative summarization evaluation
